issues.message: The sodium_first CTE partitions by le.hadm_id rather than le.stay_id; if a patient has multiple ICU stays within the same hospitalization, the first sodium across all stays is selected and could be assigned to a later stay whose own 24-h window contains no sodium, misclassifying exposure
issues.evidence: sodium_first uses PARTITION BY le.hadm_id and the cohort join is ON s.hadm_id = sf.hadm_id AND sf.rn = 1
issues.proposed_change: Change the partition and join to stay_id: PARTITION BY le.stay_id in sodium_first and ON s.stay_id = sf.stay_id in the cohort join; this is a no-op for the current first-stay-per-patient cohort but makes the query correct if the unit of analysis ever changes

issues.message: 14.6% of in-hospital deaths (966 of 6592) occur before the 24-h exposure window closes, meaning those patients may have died before a sodium could plausibly be drawn or before the "first" sodium truly represents the admission value; the primary OR of 1.452 is therefore partly driven by patients who were already dying at the time of measurement
issues.evidence: timing.events_before_exposure_window_end = 966, frac 0.1465; primary OR 1.452 vs sensitivity OR 1.463
issues.proposed_change: The 24-h landmark sensitivity (OR 1.463) already addresses this; report it as the primary robustness check and note in limitations that the primary estimate includes early deaths whose sodium may reflect terminal physiology rather than admission status

issues.message: The exclusion of 1,964 stays (3.0%) for lacking sodium within 24 h is small and plausible for a US academic ICU where basic metabolic panels are drawn on admission; however the limitations section states 43.5% excluded, which contradicts the result card (retained_frac 0.97)
issues.evidence: flow: 65366 to 63402, retained_frac 0.97; limitations text says 43.5% excluded
issues.proposed_change: Correct the limitations text to state approximately 3.0% excluded

issues.message: The URGENT admission-type category shows a higher mortality rate (13.5%) than EMERGENCY (12.1%), which is counterintuitive; this likely reflects case-mix differences (e.g. urgent transfers from other facilities with higher acuity) rather than a coding error, but is worth noting
issues.evidence: table1 admission_type URGENT outcome_rate 0.135 vs EMERGENCY 0.121
issues.proposed_change: No SQL change needed; add a brief note in limitations that URGENT captures a heterogeneous group including inter-facility transfers

issues.message: The protocol says "first serum sodium value recorded in the ICU" but does not specify whether to pool chemistry (itemid 50983) and blood-gas (itemid 50824) sodium items; the SQL pools both, which is the sensible default per dataset notes
issues.proposed_change: No change needed; document in the spec that both chemistry and blood-gas sodium are pooled per dataset guidance

waiver_decisions.quote: First serum sodium value recorded in the ICU within 24 hours of ICU admission, below 135 mmol/L ... In-hospital death (hospital_expire_flag = 1)
waiver_decisions.reason: The protocol explicitly fixes a 24-h exposure window starting at ICU admission and defines the outcome as in-hospital death from time zero, so the overlap is mandated by the protocol; the planner has added a 24-h landmark sensitivity analysis as required
